subject: english-literature
title: Said and Orientalism
welcome_lead: Edward Said's 1978 book reframed the humanities. Step into the founding text of post-colonial studies.
meta_desc: Edward Said's Orientalism (1978) at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You have read with Said — and seen how knowledge production sustained empire.

concepts.def: Edward Said's foundational study — Western academic and aesthetic representations of 'the East' produced and supported colonial power.
Said borrows Foucault's idea that knowledge and power are inseparable — discourse produces what it claims to describe.
Said's term for the symbolic mapping of self and other onto territory.
Said distinguishes the persistent unconscious orientalist substrate from its surface manifestations.
The discursive construction of a group as different and inferior — a key post-colonial mechanism.
Said's sequel reading canonical novels (Mansfield Park, Heart of Darkness) for their imperial assumptions.

walkthroughs.body_html: Said draws on Foucault: discourses do not merely describe the world but produce it. The Western knowledge of 'the Orient' was a vast machinery sustaining empire.
Said reads novels, scholarship and travel writing as a single archive. The 'Orient' that emerges is Europe's mirror — exotic, sensual, irrational — a construction Europe needed.
In his 1993 sequel, Said reads Austen's Mansfield Park against the off-stage sugar plantations of Antigua. Canonical English fiction is always also imperial fiction.
